source_name: IFC Project Disclosure Portal (disclosures.ifc.org)
why_relevant: IFC is contractually obliged to publish a Summary of Investment Information (SII) before Board approval for every investment, including its Ukrainian bank exposures (PrivatBank, Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine, Ukrgasbank, ProCredit). SII pages give counterparty legal name, instrument type, size, ownership, use of proceeds and E&S category — often the earliest public confirmation of a bank-level transaction, ahead of the bank's own disclosure.

source_name: EBRD Project Summary Documents (PSD) search / project portal
why_relevant: EBRD PSDs are the mandatory pre-signing factual summary of each project. Filterable by country=Ukraine, sector=Financial Institutions, project type (Investment vs Technical Cooperation), and status. This is the canonical register of EBRD equity stakes, risk-sharing facilities, guarantees and trade-finance lines to Ukrainian banks, plus TC projects with the NBU on financial-sector strategy and payments.

source_name: EBRD news and press releases — Ukraine financial institutions
why_relevant: EBRD announces Ukrainian bank transactions (guarantee programmes with PrivatBank, Ukrgasbank, Raiffeisen, OTP, ProCredit, Kredobank; equity funds such as Dragon Capital Rebuild Ukraine Fund) with headline volumes, EU first-loss structure and named counterparties. Faster and more candid than issuer IR during wartime; also carries annual Ukraine deployment totals (EUR 2.9bn in 2025, EUR 10.5bn cumulative wartime).

source_name: IMF Ukraine country page and Staff Country Reports (EFF reviews, Article IV)
why_relevant: IMF EFF review staff reports carry the most systematic public dataset on Ukrainian banking: financial soundness indicators tables, capital/liquidity ratios, NPLs, net interest margin, sovereign exposure share of bank assets, bank-resolution and state-bank-privatisation structural benchmarks. Programme conditionality doubles as a forward calendar of banking-sector reform.

source_name: IMF eLibrary (Ukraine staff country reports, structured)
why_relevant: Machine-friendlier XML/HTML rendering of the same IMF Ukraine staff reports, easier to parse than PDF for FSI tables and Memorandum of Economic and Financial Policies annexes.

source_name: NBU publication of the Memorandum on Economic and Financial Policies (Ukrainian translation)
source_subtype: central bank republication of IMF programme document
why_relevant: The NBU and MoF publish Ukrainian translations of the Letter of Intent / Memorandum про економічну та фінансову політику agreed with the IMF. These carry banking-sector commitments (state bank strategy, NPL resolution, DGF/Фонд гарантування вкладів reform) in the local terminology used by Ukrainian regulators and media — essential for local-language matching.

source_name: Ministry of Finance of Ukraine — IFI cooperation pages (ЄБРР / Світовий банк / МВФ / ЄІБ)
why_relevant: The MoF maintains per-IFI landing pages with cumulative portfolio figures, the list of active sovereign and sovereign-guaranteed projects, and links to project documents. It is the authoritative Ukrainian-side roster of which IFI money is in the system and under what agreement, and it supplies the Ukrainian official names of the institutions (ЄБРР, МФК, ЄІБ, БАГІ, МБРР).

source_name: World Bank Projects & Operations portal — Ukraine financial sector
why_relevant: Project pages carry Program Documents, Implementation Status Reports and ICRs for Ukraine financial-sector DPLs and jobs/private-sector operations. These documents describe deposit-guarantee-fund reform, bank resolution, state bank governance and credit-infrastructure conditions with explicit prior actions and results indicators.

source_name: World Bank Documents & Reports (documents.worldbank.org)
why_relevant: Full-text archive of World Bank analytical work on Ukrainian banking and payments — sector notes, corporate governance surveys of the banking sector, financial inclusion diagnostics — retrievable back to the 1990s and covering periods where issuer disclosure is thin.

source_name: World Bank Group donor financing mechanisms for Ukraine (ADVANCE, SURE, F.O.R.T.I.S. trust funds)
why_relevant: Explains the trust-fund and guarantee plumbing (ADVANCE Ukraine TF, SURE TF, F.O.R.T.I.S. FIF) that underwrites IFC/MIGA/IBRD risk in Ukrainian banks. Needed to interpret why a given bank transaction was possible and who bears first loss.

source_name: MIGA — Ukraine response and guarantee project briefs
why_relevant: MIGA issues political-risk guarantees directly to banks operating in Ukraine — notably cover on mandatory reserves held at the NBU against expropriation risk for ProCredit Bank Ukraine and peers, and the DFC-MIGA PRI framework for the US-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund. Project briefs name the guarantee holder, the bank, the amount and the covered risk, which is a direct read on foreign parent-bank capital commitment to Ukraine.

source_name: EIB press releases and project list — Ukraine
why_relevant: EIB and EIF disclose EU4Business Guarantee Facility agreements with named Ukrainian banks (PrivatBank, Ukreximbank, Ukrgasbank, ProCredit, plus seven-bank tranches), including guarantee size and expected mobilised lending. EIB also runs a public project register with pre-approval publication requirements.

source_name: U.S. DFC press releases and Ukraine transactions
why_relevant: DFC discloses equity and debt commitments touching Ukrainian financial services — Horizon Capital Growth Fund IV, the US-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund (URIF) seeded at USD 75m, and the DFC-MIGA political-risk-insurance framework. DFC is also statutorily required to post project-level information ahead of board consideration.

source_name: Early Warning System (ewsdata.rightsindevelopment.org) — IFI project aggregator
source_subtype: NGO aggregator / archive of IFI disclosures
why_relevant: Civil-society mirror that scrapes and archives IFC, EBRD, EIB, WB and ADB project disclosures into a stable, uniformly structured record. Extremely useful because IFI portals silently revise or retire pages; EWS preserves the original disclosure text and dates, e.g. Ukrgasbank Support (IFC-41132) with its debt-to-equity conversion option, and RSF PrivatBank (IFC-50956).

source_name: Ukraine Donor Coordination Platform
why_relevant: G7-established coordination body whose members include the WB, EBRD, EIB, IMF and IFC. Its private-sector workstream, together with the KSE Institute, publishes a compendium of IFI/DFI financing and de-risking instruments available for Ukraine across 25 countries — a single map of who offers what to Ukrainian banks, and a pointer to institutions outside the obvious five.

source_name: OpenAid Ukraine (openaid.gov.ua) — aid transparency portal
why_relevant: Ukrainian government portal intended to consolidate all IFI- and donor-supported development projects in Ukraine into one searchable register with Ukrainian project titles and implementing agencies — the local-language crosswalk between an EBRD/IFC project code and how the project is named in Ukrainian official and press usage.

source_name: EBRD-Ukraine Stabilisation and Sustainable Growth Multi-Donor Account (MDA)
source_subtype: IFI donor fund reporting / independent evaluation
why_relevant: The MDA is the donor vehicle behind much EBRD technical assistance, first-loss guarantees and concessional funding in Ukraine, including financial-sector policy work. Its annual reports and independent evaluations state which instruments were actually deployed versus merely available, giving a candid read on donor appetite for bank risk.

source_name: EU4Business–EBRD Credit Line Ukraine programme site
why_relevant: Operational programme site for EBRD/EU credit lines routed through Ukrainian partner banks. Publishes the list of participating banks, programme documents (e.g. the Financial Inclusion Recovery Programme under the Ukraine Investment Framework) and eligibility terms in Ukrainian — the bank-level distribution layer that the EBRD PSD only names in the abstract.

source_name: IFC Ukraine country page
why_relevant: Portfolio-level framing for IFC's Ukraine engagement: committed volumes, the Economic Resilience Action (ERA) programme under which most bank risk-sharing facilities sit, and links to advisory work on credit reporting and financial inclusion that touches payments infrastructure.

source_name: Ukrainian partner-bank pages describing IFI programmes (e.g. Ukreximbank EBRD programme page)
source_subtype: issuer republication of IFI programme terms
why_relevant: Ukrainian banks publish their own Ukrainian-language descriptions of IFI facilities (ЄБРР, ЄІБ, МФК, Світовий банк lines) including limits, tenors and eligible borrowers. This is the mirror image of the IFI disclosure and reveals terms and local naming the IFI page omits; Ukreximbank also hosts archived World Bank project documents in Ukrainian.

source_name: Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine — IFI co-investment platform announcements
why_relevant: The government announces the annual coordination of cooperation directions with the EBRD and European development finance institutions under the co-investment platform (Платформа співінвестування), signalling upcoming IFI activity in the financial sector before project disclosure appears.
